question: Should OpenClaw add dynamic ack reaction selection, and if so should the contract be a configured emoji array, deterministic/random selector, rule-based strategy, or model-driven pre-ack hook?
rationale: This changes a shipped cross-channel config/API surface, and ack reactions are emitted before normal reply generation, so code inspection cannot choose the user-facing semantics or compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Approve shared selector contract
options.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction`/`ackReactions` or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

options.title: Keep single-value ack reactions
options.body: Close or defer this direction and keep variability to manual message-tool reactions and lifecycle status reactions.

options.title: Defer to plugin API design
options.body: First design a plugin/channel hook for pre-ack selection if maintainers want extension-owned behavior rather than core config semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve shared selector contract
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction`/`ackReactions` or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the shared ack helper surface and prior review context for this issue.
